references.text: Jesus' prayer where he asks the Father to glorify him so that he may glorify the Father, and where he speaks of the glory he had with the Father before the world existed.
Jesus proclaims that the hour has come for the Son of Man to be glorified, and the Father answers with a voice from heaven confirming that he has already glorified him and will do so again.
Jesus discusses with the Jews who glorifies him, and he confirms that it is the Father who glorifies him, even though they do not know him.
Jesus says that Lazarus' sickness is not unto death but for God's glory, so that the Son of God may be glorified through what happens.
The description of the Word becoming flesh and dwelling among us, and we saw his glory, a glory as of an only begotten from the Father, full of grace and truth.
